text:
raj: quick sync — we need a clear mapping from Free/Pro/Enterprise plans to enforcement semantics. specifically: per-org vs per-key precedence, burst windows, and what the console shows for throttled calls.

lisa: +1. TL;DR proposal: free = per-key hard cap + short burst; pro = per-org softcap with per-key shaping; enterprise = per-org hardcap with reserved burst budget.

matt: can we be explicit about units? we enforce both token-rate and concurrent-streams. proposal: tokens/min + 1s token-bucket burst. fallback to lower-tier model when capacity exhausted.

sophia: telemetry note — we need to tag every throttle event with plan_id, org_id, key_id, route, model_variant. otherwise QA on regressions is impossible. also surface recent throttle histogram in Console (last 24h).

raj: here's a small example of the policy object I sketched (pseudo config):

```
{
  "plan": "pro",
  "enforcement": {
    "per_org": { "rate_tokens_per_min": 300000, "burst_tokens": 5000 },
    "per_key": { "rate_tokens_per_min": 60000, "burst_tokens": 1000, "hard": true },
    "fallback": "model-small-v1"
  }
}
```

lisa: that looks good. question: for free keys, do we want a silent drop or 429 + Retry-After? my vote: 429 so clients get measurable signal. :+1:

matt: 429 with `x-rate-limit-retry-after` header. also emit metric `quota.denied` with dimension plan and reason.

sophia: UX ask — Console should show: current consumption vs softcap (pro), burst consumed, and historical denied events. also an affordance to request temporary burst increase (this ties to sales).

raj: implementation concern: ordering of checks. I suggest check sequence: 1) per-org reserved capacity 2) per-key hard caps 3) per-org softcap with shaping. that lets enterprise reservations trump key-level limits when configured.

lisa: edge case — shared api keys in orgs with mixed plans. we should evaluate key->plan mapping precedence. maybe plan follows org unless key explicitly created under a different billing entity.

matt: agreed. add a lookup step: if key.plan != null then use key.plan else use org.plan. log both in telemetry.

ops-bot: quota-service v2 deployed to staging (sha: 1a2b3c). running integration tests for per-org/per-key ordering.

raj: next steps: (1) finalize JSON schema for policies (matt/lisa) (2) add telemetry tags and schema (sophia) (3) Console mocks for denied/burst (lisa). aiming for canary in staging next week.

lisa: I'll iterate on Console mock tomorrow and put in #design.

sophia: I'll draft the telemetry schema and share sample dashboards.

matt: I'll PR the enforcement ordering and add unit tests for the edge cases lisa mentioned.

raj: thanks all — adding action items to the ticket. :rocket:
